title: The distance between two functions

prereqs.why: The supremum norm turns two functions into one number, and that number is what is being asked for.
The distance is the norm of the difference, so the first move is to write down the difference.

statement:
Work in $\bigl(C[0,1], \|\cdot\|_\infty\bigr)$, the continuous real functions
on $[0,1]$ with

$$\|h\|_\infty = \sup_{t \in [0,1]} |h(t)|.$$

Let $f(t) = t^2$ and $g(t) = t^4$.

Give the exact value of $\|f - g\|_\infty$.
hints: The distance is the supremum of $|f(t) - g(t)|$, so write that difference down as a single function of $t$ first.
On $[0,1]$ the difference $t^2 - t^4$ is never negative, so the absolute value can be dropped and you are maximising an ordinary polynomial.
Differentiate $t^2 - t^4$ and set it to zero. One of the critical points is an endpoint value of 0; the other is where the maximum is, and you need the value there, not the point.

payload.prompt: The supremum distance between the two functions.
payload.label: $\|f - g\|_\infty =$
payload.syntax: A number or a fraction. 1/4 and 0.25 are the same answer.
